en: Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was on Vulture Peak Mountain by the side of the Jī River.
When he preached this Dharma, eighty-four thousand people were present; they were all arhats whose outflows were exhausted and who were no longer subject to rebirth.
The afflictions are exhausted; the fetters of all existence are severed;
what was to be done has been accomplished.
At that time, the fourfold assembly of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās gathered together;
they all assembled to listen to the Dharma,
filled with joy, and joined their palms in reverence.
With single-minded devotion, they performed prostrations and departed. At that time,
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva rose from his seat, adjusted his robes,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and joined his palms in reverence.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, after the parinirvāṇa of Śākyamuni and before Maitreya has appeared in the world,
sentient beings may have doubts."
"How should it be explained?
We pray that the Buddha will analyze and explain it.
The Buddha said:
"You should listen with a sincere mind;
I shall explain it to you in detail.
My original source may well be the body of Dīpaṃkara."
Or it may be the body of the Buddha Kūṭāgāraśikhara;
or the body of the Buddha Aprabhāsa-rāja;
or the body of the Buddha Ratnaśrī.
Or he may manifest as the body of King of Clear Enlightenment Buddha,
or as the body of Honored King of Mount Sumeru Buddha,
or as the body of Śākyamuni.
When I was originally a bodhisattva,
my name was Ajita.
After the parinirvāṇa of Śākyamuni, [I...]
First, he shall rule as a Dharma King;
thirty years later,
Maitreya will descend in person.
If there is anything you doubt, it has been explained in brief.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, how can all sentient beings cultivate merit so as to be able to see Maitreya Buddha?"
Maitreya said:
"Good sons and good daughters,
shave off your hair and beard, leave the household life, and study the Way."
Those who don the dharma robes and dwell in seclusion within the mountains and forests,
practicing meditation and studying the Way through the ascetic practices of *dhūta*,
such persons shall be able to behold Maitreya.
If there is a son of good family who distances himself from affection and love, leaves home and abandons the worldly life,
shaves off his hair and beard, and dons the dharma robes.
With single-minded ascetic practice, he skillfully expounds the Dharma for others;
through skillful conduct and transformation, he teaches the ten wholesome paths of action;
he exhorts people to receive the precepts and extensively expounds upon them.
Out of compassion and pity, they deliver others from birth and death;
they give rise to the unsurpassed mind of bodhicitta and rescue those in peril and distress.
Such are the practices of these Bodhisattvas, such are these True Persons (satpuruṣa).
They shall also behold Maitreya.
Noble sons and noble daughters,
if there are those who construct stūpas, towers, temples, lecture halls, monasteries, or images of the scriptures;
Whether one uses large or small gold, silver, or plain gilded materials,
according to the size of the image, those who quickly achieve this and make the supreme vow shall likewise behold Maitreya.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who,
along mountain paths, construct wide rest-houses and public wells,
or by riversides, build floating bridges to rescue and aid those in distress.
Those who have made such sublime vows shall likewise behold Maitreya.
Furthermore, there are sons and daughters of good family who cultivate and maintain the five precepts and practice the ten wholesome deeds.
Observing the six fast days of the month and the three long periods of fasting of the year,
they preach the Dharma for others to deliver them as well as themselves, delivering both self and others.
Such is the mind of even a hair’s breadth.
Those who have made such supreme vows for enlightenment,
as well as those individuals like them, shall also behold Maitreya.
Furthermore, if there are bhikṣus who have shaved off their hair and beards and donned the dharma robes.
Though one may receive the two hundred and fifty precepts, if one cannot maintain them in their full form,
it is not as good as receiving and upholding the ten precepts and practicing the observance of the ten wholesome actions;
even better than wearing exquisite robes is to single-mindedly engage in ascetic practice.
Do not give rise to defiled thoughts; remain far removed from affectionate attachments.
Cultivate the ten wholesome actions and practice asceticism with single-minded devotion.
[Carry] a rope bed, a mendicant’s staff, an incense burner, a water flask, and an alms bowl.

Every ninety days they would move their residence; throughout the first and last watches of the night, whether in light or darkness, they performed prostrations and practiced the Way during the six periods of the day.
They maintained the practice of eating only one meal at midday, never failing to advance their resolve.
He traveled from village to village preaching for the sake of others;
chanting in the morning and reciting in the evening, he rescued and delivered all living beings,
instructing the ignorant and leading them out of the mire of defilement.
I lead sentient beings so that they may emerge from their afflictions.
Foolish sentient beings burn within the burning house of their own ignorance, yet they do not realize it myself;
I dispatch skilled teachers to guide and transform them.
Through skillful means, he preaches the Dharma so that they may emerge from the burning house;
far removed from birth and death, they encounter an enlightened teacher,
just as a sick person encounters an excellent and effective medicine.
The patient recovers and is free from suffering and affliction.
Likewise, by upholding the precepts, repenting, and practicing asceticism with single-minded devotion, one eliminates transgressions;
thus, all develop faith and refrain from committing any evil deeds.
May they make excellent vows to enter the unsurpassed path of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
uphold and protect it, and sever all afflictions.
Such persons shall before long attain the Way and all behold Maitreya.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, you who uphold and grasp the True Dharma, skillfully govern and protect it,
rescuing and delivering those who are afflicted by illness and those in peril."
Those who uphold this sutra shall have their illnesses cured.
If there are those who are unjustly prosecuted by officials, dragged away, bound in shackles and manacles, or imprisoned,
they should keep the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra in mind.
After reciting this sutra one hundred and nine times,
he caused that official to immediately give rise to a heart of compassion;
he further issued a general amnesty, releasing them from their shackles and fetters.
They shall attain freedom from untimely death and official oppression, and be devoid of all suffering.

If there are sentient beings who travel afar and do not return, with no news reaching them, and who are bound by the afflictions of grief, sorrow, and the poison of suffering; [may they be liberated].
Those who recite this sutra while keeping Samantabhadra Bodhisattva in mind shall obtain all that they wish for without exception.
If there are women who long for sons or daughters, or who suffer from having few children,
they too should read and recite this sutra;
then their wishes shall be fulfilled.
If there is a woman who experiences difficulty in childbirth,
she should keep Samantabhadra Bodhisattva in mind and,
morning and evening, pay homage to him while receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting this sutra.
The child will give birth easily;
they will be a son of upright body and long life, possessing eloquence and valor,
attaining high advancement, wealth, and honor, and being revered and glorious for generation after generation.
All of this is due to the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
If there are sentient beings who, after their passing, encounter fire or water, being burned or swept away;
or if birds shriek, hundreds of strange omens appear, or wild insects enter their homes.
If one does not inquire about such portents with heterodox teachers,
but instead single-mindedly and diligently upholds, maintains, reads, and recites this sutra,
all clouds of evil will be dispelled and all myriad virtues will be fully prepared.
Medicines do not affect their bodies, and they remain far from the need for needles or moxibustion;
all this is due to the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
If there are good men or good women who...
Whether they be renunciants or householders,
whether laypeople or monastics,
many suffer from afflictions and distress, experiencing inverted dreams at night.
Moving in and out of a state of terror and oppression, crying out and losing track of what precedes and follows,
they keep the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra in mind and recite this sutra.
That they are free from all afflictions, that their bodies are at peace, and that they do not behold any suffering—
all this is due to the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
If there are good sons or good daughters who have made such vows, [they shall attain these benefits].
Recalling Samantabhadra Bodhisattva in one’s mind and upholding and reciting [this teaching],
one shall experience no suffering while coming and going or entering and exiting.
In every lifetime, one shall encounter the Dharma and meet with virtuous spiritual friends, never undergoing untimely or accidental suffering.
All this is due to the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. For what reason?
Because Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is the excellent medicine for the illnesses of Jambudvīpa.
This sutra is a bridge across the calamities of Jambudvīpa.
For what reason?
Because this sutra is the excellent physician for illness.
That all such upholding occurs is entirely through the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, you wish to speak a mantra for the sake of sentient beings."
Recite "Namo Buddha" three times, and then recite the names of the nine Buddhas:
the Buddha King Radiance of the East;
the Buddha Purple Sand Free from Defilement of the South.
The Buddha Immeasurable Flower in the western quarter;
the Buddha King of Sun-Turning Radiance in the northern quarter;
and the Tathāgata Fragrant Accumulation in the zenith.
The Buddha Adorned with Billions of Lions Below;
the Buddha Adorned with Billions of Vajra-Lions;
the Buddha King of Mountains of Universal Radiance and Merit.
The Buddha King of the Jewel-Treasury of Well-Abiding Merit.
If there are good sons or good daughters who receive,
uphold, read, and recite the names of these nine Buddhas, [they shall obtain great merit].
May they not fall into untimely death nor encounter the eight difficulties,
out of compassion for all sentient beings. Thereupon,
one should invoke the names of the Seven Buddhas.
The first was Vipaśyin Buddha;
the second, Viśvabhū Buddha;
the third, Śikhin Buddha.
The fourth was Krakucchanda Buddha;
the fifth was Kanakamuni Buddha;
the sixth was Kāśyapa Buddha.
Seventh is Śākyamuni Buddha.
If any sentient beings are in the midst of illness and suffering,
or if they are in the midst of distress and calamity.
Whether amidst a great conflagration,
among tigers and wolves in mountain valleys,
or upon perilous paths beset by bandits and thieves.
If one is in danger or distress by a river,
one should constantly recite the names of the Seven Buddhas;
all calamities will be completely extinguished.
For what reason?
Because this sutra abounds in spiritual powers;
it contains the dharani mantras spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas of the past and long ago.
Namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya, namaḥ saṃghāya. Namo Amitābhāya buddhāya. Sadāvara bodhi sarva mahāsattvāryaṇavarāya. Sarva prātimokṣa buddhabuddhotpāda tiriśaha kāśyapa. And he spoke this mantra:
Out of compassion for all sentient beings who are afflicted by illness,
he further invokes the names of the kings of the four continents:
"Homage to the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra of the East."
The Heavenly King Virūḍhaka of the south,
the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa of the west,
and the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa of the north.
Homage to King Dakāmagiri. To Śakra and Brahmā, the Heavenly Kings of the upper direction.
To the Cakravartin, the Holy Wheel-Turning King of the lower direction.
The Sāgara Dragon King,
the Aśura Wheel-King atop Mount Sumeru,
the various kings of the ghost spirits, and so forth.
They shall bind all ghosts and chain all ghosts;
they shall bind and chain all ghost-spirits so that they cannot approach recklessly.
O sons and daughters of good family!
When wishing to recite this mantra, one should properly observe the five precepts,
refrain from consuming alcohol, meat, or the five pungent herbs,
and maintain the six monthly fasts and the two annual long fasts.
If one practices the path with single-minded austerity during the six periods of the day, one may recite this mantra;
if one does not do so, but instead engages in various unwholesome actions, [one shall not].
If one does not recite this mantra and does not cultivate the ten virtuous actions,
this mantra will instead bring harm upon oneself.
By practicing the ten wholesome actions,
the deities of the four heavens who have renounced the world, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, and the eight classes of gods, dragons,
and spirits will constantly come to protect those who receive and uphold this mantra.
All have attained the path of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
For the sake of sentient beings, he has spoken the names of various ghosts and spirits.
If there is a ghost named Ulūpīva...
If there are pīṭhaka spirits,
if there are kumbhāṇḍa spirits,
or if there are piśāca spirits.
If there are those who inquire about or invite spirits,
I shall explain for the sake of sentient beings the names of ghosts and gods:
as for the "local deities," they are the foxes and badgers.
The mountain deity is the centipede and the python;
the house deity is the rat and the bat;
the celestial deity is Māra.
If there are ghosts coming from the east;
if there are ghosts coming from the southeast;
if there are ghosts coming from the south.
If there are ghosts coming from the southwest;
if there are ghosts coming from the west;
if there are ghosts coming from the northwest.
If there are ghosts coming from the north;
if there are ghosts coming from the northeast;
if there are flying corpse-ghosts (*veśī*) from above.
If there are ghosts lurking below;
if there are gods of heaven or gods of earth;
if there are mountain deities, tree deities, or ghosts.
Whether there be spirits and ghosts of the five paths of rebirth,
or spirits of the Southern Dipper and Northern Pole,
or spirits who seize away the vital essence of humans.
There may be ghosts who seize the vital essence of people;
there may be ghosts who snatch away the souls and spirits of people;
there may be ghosts who summon the soul-spirits of people.
If there are household-destroying spirits;
if there are spirits encountered during mourning or those that cause fire;
or if there are blue-colored spirits.
If there are white-colored spirits,
if there are yellow-colored spirits,
or if there are red-colored spirits.
If there are malevolent spirits with poisonous essences;
if there are spirits who are alternately wrathful and joyful;
if there are spirits who seek wine and meat.
If there are ghosts who crave wine or meat;
if there are ghosts who enter into people's heads;
or if there are ghosts who enter into people's ears.
If there are spirits that enter a person's mouth;
if there are spirits that enter a person's ten fingers;
or if there are spirits that enter a person's hands and feet.
If there are ghosts that enter the liver, heart, and five viscera;
if there are ghosts that enter the hundred joints;
or if there are deceitful and fraudulent ghosts.
Whether there be those who falsely claim to be ghosts,
those who are ghosts by name only,
or those who are ghosts of the seven paths.
If there are the hundred strange ghosts of the four-week period,
or the lingering corpse ghosts of the hundred-day period,
or if one suffers from illness and pain, one should recite the names of these ghosts and spirits.
If there are those who are small, weak, or difficult to nourish, one should recite the names of these spirits and deities.
If a child cries out in fear, one should likewise recite the names of these spirits and deities.
If these spirits and deities do not comply with this incantation, [they shall suffer].
Their heads shall be split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree;
the grave crime of murdering one's parents shall cause all the ghosts and spirits to treat them as if they were oil-pressing criminals;
their heads shall be split into seven pieces like fine dust.
Good sons and good daughters who receive and uphold the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts,
and who properly maintain the practice of the Ten Wholesome Paths of Action.
These spirits and deities will be unable to cause harm.
For what reason?
Because the majestic spiritual power of this great dhāraṇī mantra is inconceivable.
These various evil vapors shall not be able to harass or approach;
neither shall the various malevolent ghosts be able to inflict harm upon them.
Thus spoke Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who are able to skillfully uphold and protect this mantra,
at that time I shall mount a white elephant with six tusks and descend from the sky, raining down precious lotus flowers.
Furthermore, all other devas, benevolent spirits, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings all assembled;
they knelt on their right knees with palms joined and adjusted their robes as this great dhāraṇī mantra was being recited.
The trichiliocosm shook in six ways;
the non-Buddhists and celestial Māras all came to submit and take refuge;
even the mountains could be toppled by his incantations.
The rivers of mantras can be exhausted;
the sun and moon may fall;
and the trichiliocosm may quake in six ways.
The various māras were crushed and shattered like fine dust;
all the māras were struck with terror and submitted without exception.
Good sons and good daughters [should know this].
For those who receive and uphold this dhāraṇī mantra,
I shall at that time dispatch various celestial deities and benevolent spirits to constantly come and provide protection;
they shall not meet with untimely death.
When they themselves are about to pass away,
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva will welcome their spirit so that it does not fall into the eight difficult rebirths,
and they shall attain birth in the eastern land of Akṣobhya Buddha.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, what kind of people are unable to see Maitreya?
The Buddha said:
Excellent, excellent! Listen attentively.
Now I shall briefly explain it for you.
The first is the renunciant śramaṇa, who has shaved off his hair and beard.
Those who merely wear the dyed dharma-robes without maintaining the complete marks of a practitioner;
who do not sever their attachment to affection and instead turn their backs on the Dharma to fall back into secular life—
such persons shall not behold Maitreya.
Second, there are those who have left the household life as śramaṇas and shaved off their hair and beards,
yet merely don the dharma robes in pretense to evade official corvée labor;
they drink alcohol and eat meat.
They delight in blue, yellow, red, and white, and in fine adornments.
They ride donkeys and horses, with their *kāṣāya* robes tied around their waists.
They engage in livelihoods such as trading, skillfully manipulating measures and bushels, and fiddling with scales from beginning to end.
To use a large bushel or a heavy scale is called "stealing by means of a kalpa";
to use a small scale or a small bushel is called "theft.
In this way, such śramaṇas will not see Maitreya.
Third, there are those who have left the household life as śramaṇas and shaved off their hair and beards,
yet falsely don the Dharma robes while drinking alcohol, eating meat,
breaking the precepts by eating at night, and stealing from the Three Jewels.
They destroy the Three Jewels and do not maintain the complete marks;
they commit various improper acts.
Such are their evil deeds.
Such people as these will likewise not see Maitreya.
Fourth, there are sentient beings with roots of goodness who uphold the five precepts,
yet they are unwilling to study and recite them, thereby damaging and destroying the True Dharma.
Those who believe in heterodox views and inverted perspectives, who engage in all manner of improper conduct,
and who violate the five precepts with their six sense faculties in a state of perversion—
such persons as these shall not behold Maitreya.
Fifth, although he had received and upheld the five precepts,
by means of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, he traveled to various regions to preach and convert others,
yet he destroyed Buddhist images.
They destroy the great to make it small,
and destroy the small to make it great;
they deface and destroy images, and bring about the ruin and extinction of the Triple Gem.
Such a person likewise does not see Maitreya.
Sixth, one who upholds the pure precepts yet violates the ten wholesome actions and breaks these various precepts [does not see him].
Those who drink alcohol, eat meat, and commit various unwholesome deeds— by destroying these three evils—
such persons likewise shall not see Maitreya.
Seventh, if there are foolish sentient beings who do not believe in the Triple Gem.
They slander and revile the True Dharma; they slander and revile the community of bhikṣus;
they slander and revile upāsakas and upāsikās.
They slander and revile the Three Jewels and the four classes of noble ones, obstructing the Tathāgata’s Right Path and severing the continuity of the Three Jewels.
Such persons as these shall likewise not behold Maitreya.
Eighth, if there are sentient beings who block the royal highways of officials and kings,
destroy households, plunder, and set fire to mountains and marshes.
Those who kill living beings and lack a heart of compassion—
such people as these shall also not behold Maitreya.
Ninth, if there are sentient beings who have risen high to wealth and honor as ministers who assist the state;
They rely on the power and influence of their official positions to adjudicate matters unjustly;
they turn the straight into the crooked and magnify the small into the great,
falsely slaying the virtuous and thereby seizing control over the myriad people.
Such persons as these shall likewise not behold Maitreya.
Tenth, it is for this reason that I speak thus to you:
if there are those, whether laypeople or monastics, who rely on the white [dharma] yet commit these various evils without shame or remorse.
They are like birds, beasts, oxen, horses, and other animals;
such people enter the Avīci Hell,
circling through the five realms of existence from darkness to darkness, with no time of escape.
2. *The Sūtra on Realizing the Original Cause of Incense and Offerings*, Spoken by the Buddha. The Second [Chapter]: The Original Cause of Incense and Offerings as Taught by the Seven Buddhas.
At that time, the seven Buddhas were in the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven.
The Buddha’s chief was the Tathāgata King of Emptiness;
his foremost successor was the Buddha King of Emptiness,
and the second was the Buddha Cloud-Thunder-Sound Constellation-King-Flower-Wisdom.
The fourth was the Tathāgata Buddha Śuklodana-rāja;
the fifth was the Buddha Ratnasthita-padma;
the sixth was the Buddha Amūlarāja.
Seventh is the prediction of Maitreya as a Buddha.
Regarding the seven Buddhas, they first made their vow together in the Śvetaketu Heaven,
and again made their vow together on Vulture Peak Mountain.
Furthermore, he made a vow at Mount Ziwai and again made a vow at River Sha.
At that time, the King of Space issued a gentle decree to summon all the bodhisattvas.
To the north, there were bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges Rivers.
Each was mounted upon a six-tusked white elephant and carried precious jewels and golden lotuses in their hands as they all proceeded to the place where the Buddha was.
At that time, there were also bodhisattvas from the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges Rivers,
who likewise mounted six-tusked white elephants and came to the Buddha’s dwelling,
raining down precious lotus flowers.
At that time, there were further ten *gaṅgā*-sands of bodhisattvas from the south who also mounted six-tusked white elephants,
carrying jeweled crowns and necklaces, and came to where the Buddha was.
At that time, there were also bodhisattvas from the western direction, as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges Rivers,
who likewise mounted six-tusked white elephants and each brought various *bodhi*-flowers to the place where the Buddha was.
At that time, there were bodhisattvas from the upper direction, as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges Rivers, who,
riding upon the lion of meditative concentration and raining down precious celestial robes out of a heart of profound compassion, came to the place where the Buddha was.
At that time, those who had emerged from the earth, each wearing precious jewels upon their heads, spoke these words:
"We have heard of the joyful assembly where the Buddha has made his vow;
it is now the time for the gathering of sixty thousand bodhisattvas."
Mountains, rivers, and the great ocean shook in six ways.
At that time, the minds of the various māras were ill at ease due to the Buddha’s spiritual power and the excellence of the True Dharma.
At that time, King Śuddhodana joyfully accepted the instruction.
He and the Tathāgata Gaganarāja each spoke these words:
"There is no land of Jambudvīpa."
Sentient beings are especially without karmic conditions;
for the sake of the foremost ascetic practices of the Bodhisattvas of the Six Directions,
there is the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara, disciple of Amitāyus Buddha of the Western Quarter.
This Great Bodhisattva has a karmic affinity to rescue and deliver those in Jambudvīpa.
At that time, there was Mahāprajāpatī Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, a disciple of the Buddha Rājaprabhāsa in the eastern direction.
The merit and benefits of incense, lamps, and offerings accrue to those with a karmic connection.
These two Bodhisattvas provide rare salvation, uprooting the suffering of all sentient beings;
they provide rare benefit through their excellent teachings.
When the Tathāgata was about to depart for the Śukra Heaven to make his vow,
eighty-four thousand people accompanied him with jeweled pillars, banners, and canopies, all like brothers.
In the heavens there is a canopy, vast and infinite,
thirty yojanas in length and breadth;
it is likewise so in the east, west, above, and below.
The divine banner of the vow was thirty yojanas in length and breadth.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara took birth as an ordinary person;
at that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva appeared in the body of an upāsaka.
These two bodhisattvas are emanations;
their hundred billion [emanations] are difficult to understand, difficult to comprehend, and inconceivable.
At that time, there were the Bodhisattva Like-a-Child and the Youth Candraprabha.
At that time, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa was [the Buddha], Upāli was [Śāriputra],
and Master Tang was a *srotāpanna* arhat.
Senglang of Taishan was one who had transcended all birth and death;
Beidu was a pure arhat;
and the one known as Master Yin was an arhat who had realized emptiness.
The three levels of worthies and the four stages of holiness all share this same single word.
If you wish to expound this root, do not speak it with carelessness among those of evil nature;
rather, bestow this Dharma-root upon them.
If a person lacks roots of goodness, they shall not hear this Dharma, nor shall they be able to expound it.
They have not yet delivered those to be delivered; they have not yet heard what is to be heard, seen what is to be seen, understood what is to be understood, or known what is to be known.
Such people as these all follow from a single vow.
Regarding what the Tathāgata has spoken, there is none who does not rejoice;
they receive and uphold it with a single mind, and shall certainly obtain the fruit of their vow.
Do not remain fixed in either advancing or retreating;
thus shall the fruition of the result—the samādhi of liberation—be accomplished.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva came to the place where the Buddha was, knelt with their right knees touching the ground, and received his instructions.
I only pray that the Tathāgata will expound it for me and explain it for me.
Listen attentively, receive it with heedfulness, grasp it, and uphold it;
I shall not dare to transgress it, nor dare to omit anything, nor dare to damage it.
At that time, the Buddha said:
"In the land of Jambudvīpa, within the kingdom of Zhendan (China), the region extends east-west and north-south.
A single Buddha-field consists of ten billion Mount Sumerus, ten billion suns and moons, and ten billion oceans."
Within this trichiliocosm,
there is a great kingdom named China,
where people do not recognize the True Dharma and do not recognize the Tathāgata.
Failing to understand the True Dharma and failing to recognize virtuous people—
such sentient beings are like blind people who cannot see the sun and moon;
their lack of affinity with the Dharma is likewise so.
Suppose there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or sons and daughters of good family who either uphold,
recite, or transcribe it.
Whether upholding it, reciting it, or guarding the incense and lamps with care—
as if protecting a bright pearl—
good sons and good daughters [shall do so].

they do not need to strive, for it occurs spontaneously.
Furthermore, when desiring to receive their final end,
they shall be reborn in the Land of Immeasurable Life,
spontaneously arising from within a lotus flower.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said:
"O devas, nāgas, yakṣas,
gandharvas, and asuras."
Mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth;
bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs,
upāsakas, and upāsikās.
Good sons and good daughters shall long cultivate the ten wholesome paths and observe the three-month and six-day fasts;
with single-minded devotion they shall practice until they attain the Way of the Buddha.
At that time, after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, the ghosts and spirits will become violent and cruel. The Four Heavenly Kings [will respond].
When the World-Honored One appears in the world,
we, his retinue, shall kneel with palms joined and listen attentively and receive [his teaching] with focused attention.
They shall grasp the True Dharma,
practice it, uphold it,
and not dare to transgress it.
We shall uphold and protect it.
At that time, we and our retinues, residing upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, shall rule over the four continents.

Seeing suffering, do not avoid it;
seeing pleasure, do not crave it.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva came from the east,
bringing celestial music and raining down flowers that shook the earth.
When this person is on the verge of passing away,
their spirit will be received so that they do not encounter the eight difficulties,
and they shall attain rebirth in the eastern land of the Buddha Akṣobhya.

If one upholds this sutra and recites it one hundred times,
whatever wishes one has in one's heart will be obtained without exception.
Should one encounter officials or disputes involving verbal contention and mutual entanglement, [the same shall apply].
One should also read and recite this sutra so that even their officials may be transformed to possess a compassionate heart and be free from all evils.
If they suffer from many ailments for years on end without recovery, [they shall be healed].
They place their faith in teachers of various demonic and heterodox views who,
through divination and inquiry, seek out calamities;
they slaughter pigs, dogs, oxen, and sheep to sacrifice to ghosts and spirits.
To harbor long-standing hatred brings no ultimate benefit.
It is better to destroy the hosts of Māra, belong to the Buddha, hang silken banners and canopies, burn incense, scatter flowers, and offer songs of praise.
By reciting the *Saptasaptarātra-stotra-sūtra* and walking the path of practice for seven times seven nights, one shall be liberated from all bonds of Māra.
In all these cases, ghosts and spirits are unable to approach or draw near.
For what reason?
Because this sutra abounds in majestic spiritual power.
This is due to the majestic spiritual power of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Ānanda addressed the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra:
"If there are good sons or good daughters..."
For those who uphold and protect this sutra,
there shall be no manifold difficulties;
whether walking, coming, going, or entering, they shall constantly give rise to great loving-kindness and great compassion.
He delivers sentient beings, taking pity on their suffering and calamity, and uproots the pains of all living beings.
Ānanda said:
"He does not merely lead sentient beings by means of the Great Vehicle or the Small Vehicle to transform them."
The three vehicles employ skillful means to rescue and deliver those in peril and distress.
If there are good men or good women who give rise to even a hair’s breadth of a virtuous mind, [they shall be saved].
May you live long and encounter favorable circumstances;
may you constantly give rise to supreme vows;
and may benevolent deities protect and sustain you.
All of this is due to the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
it is as sublime as this.
Thus did Samantabhadra Bodhisattva speak to certify and elucidate this sutra.
